Exam Hints: ✓ What? India re-elected as President of ISA ✓ Term: 2026–2028 (two years) ✓ Co-President: France ✓ Announced by: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, MNRE ✓ ISA Established: 30 November 2015. ✓ Founding Countries: India and France Key Initiatives of ISA: Solar Financing: Promote solar investments through the USD 200 million Africa Solar Facility and USD 300 million Nigeria Distributed Renewable Energy (DRE) Fund, while India committed Rs. 225 crore (USD 25 million) to expand affordable solar-energy access. • The ISA also aims to support solar-powered agriculture and the global deployment of 1 million solar pumps, drawing on India’s Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM- KUSUM) scheme. Island Solar Projects: Promote solar projects in Fiji, Madagascar, Comoros and Seychelles. Develop solar and energy-storage projects in Mauritius and achieve up to 500 MW (Megawatt) of solar capacity in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) by 2030. Technology: Strengthen solar capabilities through 17 Solar Technology Application Resource Centres (STAR-Cs), the SHINE Global Capability Centre and the AI-enabled ISA Academy. About ISA: It was jointly launched by India and France on 30 November 2015, on the sidelines of the 21st Conference of the Parties (COP21) in Paris, France, to promote solar energy adoption and international cooperation under the “One Sun, One World, One Grid” (OSOWOG) principle, and had 130 signatory and member countries as of November 2026. INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS WIPO’s GII 2026: India Ranks 38th, Switzerland Retains Top Position In November 2026, the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO) released the 19th edition of “Global Innovation Index (GII 2026): Powering entrepreneurs at the frontier of science”. As per the index, India ranked at 38th spot (same as previous year) with an overall score of 40.1. • Switzerland retained the 1st position (with an overall score of 66.7) in the GII 2026 for a 16th consecutive year. Sweden and the United States of America (USA) continued to secure 2nd and 3rd positions, respectively for the 4th consecutive year.

About Global Innovation Index (GII): Index: The Gll was launched in 2007 by Professor Soumitra Dutta at INSEAD, with WIPO joining as a co- publisher in 2012 and becoming the sole publisher in 2021. Evaluation: The GII evaluated the innovation performance of 139 world economies using 79 indicators, ranging from Research & Development (R&D) spending, Venture Capital (VC) deals, high-tech exports and Intellectual Property Filings. Sub-Indices: The GII comprises of two sub-indices: • The Innovation Input Sub-Index which includes 5 pillars namely, Institutions; Human Capital and Research; Infrastructure; Market Sophistication; and Business Sophistication. • While, the Innovation Output Sub-Index has 2 pillars i.e. Knowledge and Technology Outputs and Creative Outputs. Top 5 Countries: GII 2026 Global Rank Country Name Overall Score 1 Switzerland 66.7 2 Sweden 63.2 3 The United States of America (USA) 62.3 4 Republic of Korea 61.4 5 Singapore 61.0 38 India 40.1 Bottom 5 Countries – GII 2026: Global Rank Country Overall Score 135 Burundi 15.1 136 Angola 13.0 137 Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) 12.6 138 Niger 12.1

Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 18 Daily Content PDF INS Surat Participates in 15th Edition of India-Oman Maritime Exercise ‘Naseem Al Bahr 2026’ in Oman In November 2026, the Indian Navy (IN) and the Royal Navy of Oman (RNO) commenced the 15th edition of their bilateral maritime exercise ‘Naseem Al Bahr’ (Sea Breeze) at Muscat, Oman, from 8th to 11th November 2026. • Indian Naval Ship (INS) Surat participated in the exercise, followed by a Coordinated Patrol (CORPAT), aimed at enhancing interoperability, exchanging operational experiences and strengthening mutual understanding between the two navies. Exam Hints: ✓ What? 15th India-Oman bilateral maritime exercise Naseem Al Bahr (Sea Breeze) ✓ Where? Muscat, Oman ✓ When? 8–11 November 2026 ✓ Objective: Enhance interoperability, exchange operational experiences and strengthen mutual understanding ✓ Indian Participant: Indian Naval Ship (INS) Surat. ✓ Omani Participant: Royal Navy of Oman. ✓ Phases: Harbour and sea phases ✓ Activities: Cross-deck visits, operational interactions and sporting events. Background: Origin: Naseem Al Bahr is a biennial bilateral maritime exercise between the IN and RNO, initiated in 1993, to strengthen naval cooperation and maritime security. Previous Edition: The 14th edition of the exercise was conducted between the IN and the RNO off the coast of Goa from 13 to 18 October 2024, with India participating through INS Trikand and a Dornier Maritime Patrol Aircraft, while Oman deployed RNOV Al Seeb. About Naseem Al Bahr 2026: Aim: To strengthen maritime cooperation, enhance operational interoperability and deepen professional ties between the IN and the RNO. Participants: India is represented by INS Surat, while Oman is represented by the RNO. • INS Surat is the fourth and final ship of the Visakhapatnam, class guided-missile destroyers developed under Project 15B and was commissioned into the Indian Navy(IN) on 15 January 2025. It was built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) with over 75% indigenous content. Phases: The exercise comprises two phases, • Harbour Phase: Personnel from both navies will participate in professional interactions, including cross-deck visits, operational interactions and sporting events. These engagements will facilitate the exchange of experiences and best practices. • Sea Phase: Both navies will undertake operational engagements to enhance interoperability, strengthen coordination and develop mutual understanding. Key Developments in Naseem Al Bahr 2026: Defence Cooperation: The engagement builds on the momentum generated during the 13th India–Oman Joint Military Cooperation Committee (JMCC) meeting, held in New Delhi on 24 November 2025, co-chaired by India’s Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and Oman’s Secretary General of the Ministry of Defence Dr. Mohammed bin Naseer bin Ali Al Zaabi. # Page 23^page=23
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 23 Daily Content PDF ✓ Winning Invention: Sentinel. ✓ Purpose: Detects hidden structural damage in concrete buildings after earthquakes. ✓ Prize Money: PHP 2.39 million (approximately £30,000). Highlights of the Invention: Invention: Sentinel converts a conventional concrete spacer block into a sensor that detects hidden cracks through changes in electrical resistance using self-sensing concrete. • The device uses embedded electrodes and an electronic module to detect resistance variations and wirelessly send data to an online dashboard for remote monitoring. Development: Ong tested over 125 concrete samples and installed sensors in a Philippine building; he plans further validation and versions for existing buildings.
